name: Greek Lemon Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
summary: Marinate chicken in lemon, garlic, and oregano, then roast over potatoes until golden.
technique_notes: Toss the potatoes in the same lemon-oil-oregano marinade and arrange in a single layer under the chicken so they roast in the rendered fat; roast at 425°F. Pat chicken dry and start it skin-side up for browning. Hold most of the lemon juice until the last 10 minutes so it doesn't turn bitter.

name: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Lemon and Asparagus
summary: Roast salmon and asparagus on one pan with olive oil, lemon, and herbs.
technique_notes: Roast skin-side down at 400°F, 10-15 min, pulling salmon at 120-130°F internal (instant-read) for medium-rare so it stays moist. Arrange asparagus around the perimeter, salmon in the center; match thin spears to the short cook time. Pat salmon dry and squeeze lemon on after roasting, not before.

name: Shakshuka (Eggs Poached in Spiced Tomato Sauce)
summary: Simmer peppers and tomatoes with cumin and paprika, poach eggs in the sauce, finish with feta.
technique_notes: Saute onions and peppers over high heat, mostly undisturbed (~6 min, then ~4 more), so they char and tenderize without turning sweet; add garlic, then bloom paprika and cumin 30 sec. Simmer sauce 10 min. Make wells, spoon sauce over the whites, cover on lowest heat 5-8 min until whites set, yolks runny.

name: Greek Salad with Chickpeas
summary: Toss cucumber, tomato, olives, and chickpeas with feta and a red-wine vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Rinse canned chickpeas to cut sodium. Use firm English or Persian cucumbers (thin-skinned, few seeds) so the salad holds up. Whisk the EVOO-lemon dressing in the bowl first, then toss everything to coat. Use fresh lemon over bottled for brighter flavor. Authentic Greek versions skip lettuce.

name: Mediterranean Lentil Soup
summary: Simmer green lentils with mirepoix, cumin, and tomato; stir in spinach and lemon at the end.
technique_notes: Hold the acid (lemon and most of the tomato) until the lentils are fully tender; acid added early keeps lentils hard. Soften the mirepoix first, and stir spinach in at the very end off the heat so it just wilts.

name: Mediterranean Quinoa Bowl with Feta and Cucumber
summary: Layer quinoa with chickpeas, chopped veg, feta, and a lemon-tahini drizzle.
technique_notes: Rinse quinoa well under cold water to wash off bitter saponins. Add the still-warm cooked quinoa to the lemon vinaigrette so it absorbs the dressing, then let it cool completely before stirring in the cold vegetables so they stay crisp. Top with feta last.

name: Baked Cod with Tomatoes, Olives, and Capers
summary: Bake cod in a puttanesca-style tomato, olive, and caper sauce.
technique_notes: Build the sauce on the stovetop first: saute onion (fennel) 7-9 min until soft, add garlic 1 min, then tomatoes and olives, simmering ~2 min to thicken. Pat cod dry and season, nestle it into the sauce spooning some over the top, then bake at 350°F just 6-8 min until it flakes. Go easy on salt.

name: Baked Falafel Bowls with Tahini
summary: Bake spiced chickpea falafel and serve over greens with cucumber, tomato, and tahini sauce.
technique_notes: Soak dried chickpeas (with a little baking soda) overnight, 18+ hrs, until one crushes easily; never use canned. Drain and pat very dry (excess moisture makes them gooey). Pulse coarse, not pureed, and chill 1+ hr so they hold shape without egg or flour. Oil the pan, brush tops, bake 350°F 8 min, flip, 7-12 min more.

name: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Stew
summary: Simmer white beans with kale, garlic, and tomato into a hearty rosemary-scented stew.
technique_notes: Soften onion, carrot, and celery ~8 min, then garlic 1 min. Simmer soaked beans 45-50 min until nearly tender before adding kale and tomatoes; kale needs another 30-45 min to soften. A Parmesan rind simmered in adds savory depth (freeze rinds up to 6 months). Stir in vinegar and salt only at the very end.

name: Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki
summary: Grill lemon-oregano chicken skewers; serve with cucumber-yogurt tzatziki and a chopped salad.
technique_notes: Marinate even chicken cubes in the lemon-vinegar-garlic-oregano dressing ~2 hrs, reserving some dressing (unmixed) for the salad. Salt the cucumber and drain ~30 min, then pat dry before mixing into Greek yogurt so the tzatziki stays thick. Don't crowd skewers; grill over medium-high to 155°F internal (~5 min), rest 3 min.

name: Turkey and Brown Rice Stuffed Bell Peppers
summary: Stuff peppers with spiced turkey, brown rice, and tomato; bake until tender.
technique_notes: Par-cook the rice to only ~70% since it finishes inside the peppers, and pre-soften the peppers (blanch or microwave ~5 min) so they're tender in time. Bake covered with foil first, then uncover to brown the tops.

name: Whole Wheat Pasta with Cherry Tomatoes, White Beans, and Basil
summary: Burst cherry tomatoes in olive oil and garlic, toss with pasta, white beans, and basil.
technique_notes: Blister the cherry tomatoes in hot oil without stirring much so they char and burst. Reserve starchy pasta water and toss everything off the heat to emulsify a light sauce. Fold the beans in gently at the end to keep them whole.

name: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice with Crispy Onions)
summary: Cook lentils and rice with cumin; top with deeply caramelized onions and a yogurt dollop.
technique_notes: Par-boil lentils ~10-12 min until just tender, then drain. Caramelize the diced onions deeply for about 40 min until darker than normal caramelized (this gives the golden hue), reserve thin onion rings to fry separately in shimmering oil for the crisp garnish. Rinse and soak rice, add with lentils, simmer covered 15-20 min, then rest 10 min.

name: Grilled Mediterranean Chicken Salad
summary: Slice grilled chicken over greens with cucumber, tomato, olives, and a lemon vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Pound the chicken to an even thickness so it cooks evenly, and rest it after grilling before slicing to keep it juicy. Dress the greens only just before serving.

name: Salmon Niçoise-Style Salad
summary: Compose seared salmon with blanched green beans, eggs, potatoes, and a dijon vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Cook each component to its own right doneness: blanch the green beans then shock in ice water to keep them bright and crisp, aim for jammy 7-8 minute eggs, and sear the salmon skin-side down. Compose the plate, don't toss it.

name: Tabbouleh with Grilled Chicken
summary: Toss a parsley-forward bulgur tabbouleh with lemon and olive oil; top with sliced grilled chicken.
technique_notes: It's parsley-forward with bulgur as an accent. Chop herbs by hand with a sharp knife — a food processor bruises them and turns the salad soggy. For fine bulgur, soak (don't boil) in cold water ~20 min until tender, then drain well. Flavor improves as it rests; keeps up to 3 days chilled.

name: Eggplant and Chickpea Tagine
summary: Stew eggplant and chickpeas with warm spices and a touch of dried fruit; serve over couscous or farro.
technique_notes: Salt and brown or roast the eggplant first so it isn't spongy and raw, then build the spiced base and stew gently. Add the dried fruit partway through so it plumps without dissolving.

name: Yogurt-Marinated Grilled Chicken with Farro
summary: Marinate chicken in spiced yogurt and grill; serve over farro with a herb salad.
technique_notes: Let the yogurt marinade work at least 2 hours - it tenderizes the chicken - then scrape off the excess before grilling so it chars instead of steaming. Toast the farro before simmering for a nuttier flavor.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Bowl with Brown Rice and Edamame
summary: Glaze salmon with a light teriyaki, serve over brown rice with edamame and cucumber.
technique_notes: Reduce the teriyaki to a glaze separately, brush it on only at the end, and broil 1-2 min so the sugars caramelize without scorching. Pat the salmon dry first so it sears rather than steams.

name: Thai-Inspired Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
summary: Stir-fry chicken and crisp vegetables in a garlic-ginger-fish-sauce glaze; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Cook over the highest heat in batches so the chicken sears instead of steaming. Add vegetables by density (peppers before snap peas) and stir in the basil off the heat at the very end so it stays fragrant.

name: Korean-Style Beef Bowl (Bulgogi)
summary: Sear thin-sliced marinated beef; serve over brown rice with quick-pickled cucumber and greens.
technique_notes: Slice the beef very thin against the grain (freeze 20 min first; kitchen shears help) and use grated pear or onion to tenderize. Marinate 1 hour up to 1 day. Cook in batches over medium-high heat about 5 minutes, adding a little honey at the end to caramelize; sear hard without crowding.

name: Vietnamese Chicken Lettuce Wraps
summary: Saute ground chicken with ginger and lime; spoon into lettuce cups with shredded carrot and herbs.
technique_notes: Spread the ground chicken and brown undisturbed about 6 minutes, then break up and cook 6-8 more until browned. Stir in shallots/chilies 30 seconds, then pull off heat and fold in the lime-fish-sauce-sugar mix with herbs to keep it bright. Keep filling and herbs separate from the lettuce until eating.

name: Miso-Glazed Cod with Bok Choy
summary: Broil miso-glazed cod and serve with quick-seared bok choy and brown rice.
technique_notes: Marinate the cod in the miso 4-8 hours or overnight. Cook bok choy cut-side down in oil plus a splash of water until the water evaporates and it caramelizes, 6-7 min, then add garlic and vinegar 1-2 min. Broil cod about 8 min, rotating halfway; the miso sugars char fast, so watch closely.

name: Ginger Chicken with Soba Noodles
summary: Toss seared ginger chicken and vegetables with soba in a light soy-sesame sauce.
technique_notes: Rinse the cooked soba under cold water to stop the cooking and wash off surface starch (this prevents gummy clumps), then toss with a little oil. Add the snap peas in only the last minute so they stay crisp.

name: Sesame Tofu and Broccoli Stir-Fry
summary: Crisp tofu and stir-fry with broccoli in a garlic-sesame-soy sauce over brown rice.
technique_notes: Press the tofu at least 30 min, cut into 1-inch cubes, salt, then toss with cornstarch (about 2 Tbsp) for crispness. Heat the pan before adding oil so cubes don't stick, and fry golden on each side. The cornstarch sauce thickens fast, so add broccoli, then sauce, and fold the tofu back in off the heat.

name: Black Bean and Sweet Potato Tacos
summary: Roast cumin-spiced sweet potato, fold into tortillas with black beans, avocado, and lime slaw.
technique_notes: Cut sweet potato into 1/2-inch cubes, toss with oil/chili/cumin, and roast at 425°F in a single uncrowded layer; flip at 15 min and roast 15 more until edges crisp. Warm tortillas in a dry skillet, covered to stay soft. Dress the slaw with its acid only just before serving.

name: Chicken Fajita Bowls
summary: Sear fajita-spiced chicken and peppers; build bowls with brown rice, beans, and avocado.
technique_notes: Toss chicken and peppers in spiced oil so the spices bloom in the fat. For char, sear in batches over high heat without stirring constantly; for hands-off cooking, roast on a preheated sheet at 425°F about 15 min, then add beans and finish. Rest the chicken, then slice against the grain.

name: Peruvian-Style Grilled Chicken with Green Sauce
summary: Grill cumin-lime marinated chicken; serve with a creamy yogurt-cilantro green sauce.
technique_notes: Rub with a vinegar-cumin-paprika-garlic paste and marinate at least an hour. Cook slow over indirect/cooler heat skin-side up to render fat, then finish skin-down over direct heat to crisp and char. The green sauce is blended raw (cilantro, lime, jalapeño, yogurt) - make it fresh and keep it cold.

name: Shrimp and Avocado Salad
summary: Toss poached shrimp with avocado, tomato, and a lime-cilantro dressing over greens.
technique_notes: Poach the shrimp gently just until they curl into a C and turn pink (a tight O means overcooked), then shock in ice water. Add the avocado and dress only at the last moment to prevent browning and mush.

name: Turkey and Black Bean Chili
summary: Simmer lean turkey with beans, peppers, and tomato in a smoky chili spice blend.
technique_notes: Saute onion, carrot, and pepper 6-8 min, then bloom garlic, chili powder, and cumin in the oil 1 min before liquid for depth. Lean turkey has no fat to render, so start with oil and brown about 5 min. Deglaze the browned bits, then simmer covered 30 min and uncovered 30 min to thicken.

name: Chana Masala (Chickpea Curry)
summary: Simmer chickpeas in a tomato-onion masala with ginger and warm spices; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Build a deeply browned onion-tomato-ginger-garlic masala (10+ min) before the chickpeas go in - that base is the flavor - then simmer the chickpeas in it to absorb. Finish with garam masala and lemon off the heat.

name: Tandoori-Style Chicken with Cucumber Raita
summary: Roast yogurt-and-spice marinated chicken; serve with cooling cucumber raita and brown rice.
technique_notes: Use a two-stage marinade (lemon and salt first, then yogurt and spices) and slash the thighs so it penetrates; marinate at least 2 hours. Broil in the upper third, flipping every 4 minutes until 165°F; most charring happens in the first 10 minutes. Grate, seed and drain the cucumber for the raita.

name: Red Lentil Dal with Spinach
summary: Simmer red lentils with turmeric, ginger, and tomato; wilt in spinach and finish with a spice tempering.
technique_notes: Start lentils in room-temperature water with no salt (prevents graininess); skim foam and simmer uncovered 20-30 min until creamy. Don't skip the tarka: bloom whole spices in hot ghee/oil and pour over at the end, reserving some to spoon on top. Stir spinach in last, 3-5 min.

name: Turkey Meatballs with Marinara over Whole Wheat Pasta
summary: Bake herbed turkey meatballs, simmer in marinara, and serve over whole wheat pasta.
technique_notes: Don't overmix or pack the meatballs; grated onion, egg and bread crumbs keep lean turkey moist. Brown on all sides, about 5 minutes, then pour off excess oil and finish simmering gently in the marinara 15-20 minutes so they stay tender and the flavors blend.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Sausage with Peppers and White Beans
summary: Roast chicken sausage with peppers and onions, toss with white beans and a splash of vinegar.
technique_notes: Brown the sliced sausage hard (only 1-2 min per side, then remove) and sauté aromatics in the residual fat. Drain the white beans but don't rinse them - the starchy liquid makes the sauce. Simmer beans 4-5 min, then wilt greens and return the sausage at the very end so the beans stay intact.

name: Cobb-Style Salad with Grilled Chicken
summary: Arrange grilled chicken, egg, avocado, and tomato over greens with a light vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Prep each component separately and arrange in rows, serving the vinaigrette on the side to dress at the table. Herb-rub the chicken and grill 5-6 min per side to 160°F, then rest 10 minutes before slicing. Keep avocado tossed in lemon to hold its color. Everything goes on cold.

name: Spinach and Feta Frittata
summary: Bake eggs with wilted spinach, scallions, and feta into a sliceable frittata.
technique_notes: Wilt the spinach and wring out all liquid (cheesecloth/towel) or the frittata weeps. Heat oil until shimmering so eggs don't stick, set the bottom on the stovetop about 4 min, then bake at 375°F about 8 min until the top no longer jiggles. Rest a few minutes before slicing.

name: Moroccan Salmon with Chermoula
summary: Coat salmon in a cilantro-cumin chermoula and roast; serve with couscous or farro and greens.
technique_notes: Chermoula is a raw blended herb sauce - toast the cumin and coriander seeds first, then blitz with herbs, lemon and garlic, adding water to a drizzling consistency (can be made ahead). Roast salmon skin-side down at 400°F (200C) for 15-20 min just to medium. Drizzle some over and serve the rest on the side.

name: Spanish Chickpea and Spinach Stew (Garbanzos con Espinacas)
summary: Simmer chickpeas and spinach with smoked paprika, cumin, and tomato until thick and silky.
technique_notes: Cook onion, garlic and smoked paprika in oil until softened and slightly browned before adding tomato. Wilt the spinach in a handful at a time, then simmer the chickpeas with their canned liquid (it gives body) about 30 min until thick. Finish off the heat with EVOO and a few drops of sherry vinegar.

name: Turkish White Bean Stew (Fasulye)
summary: Stew white beans with carrot, onion, and tomato paste; brighten with lemon and parsley.
technique_notes: Cook the tomato paste until it darkens and loses its raw edge before adding liquid, then simmer gently so the beans stay intact. Brighten with lemon and parsley off the heat.

name: Chicken Fattoush Salad
summary: Toss crisp greens, cucumber, tomato, and grilled chicken with a sumac-lemon dressing and toasted pita.
technique_notes: Bake split pita brushed with oil and sumac at 350F about 15 min until crisp, then break into pieces. Whisk a lemon-sumac vinaigrette, toss in the pita with the vegetables, and let stand 15 min so it soaks up dressing. Grill seasoned chicken 3-4 min per side; slice thin over the salad.

name: Baked Trout with Lemon and Herbs
summary: Roast trout with lemon, garlic, and fresh herbs; serve with a grain and greens.
technique_notes: Pat fillets dry and bake skin-side down at 400F for 10-12 min, checking at 10. Pull at about 140F internal (carryover brings it to a safe 145F) just as the flesh turns opaque and flakes. Tuck lemon and herbs over the fillets; keeping skin on holds it together. Finish with more lemon.

name: Garlic Shrimp with Zucchini and Quinoa
summary: Saute shrimp in garlic and lemon with ribboned zucchini; serve over quinoa.
technique_notes: Don't overcook the shrimp (a C shape, not a tight O). Cook the zucchini hot and fast so it doesn't go soggy and watery, and add the garlic late so it doesn't burn. Finish with lemon off the heat.

name: Greek Baked Fish (Psari Plaki)
summary: Bake white fish over a bed of stewed tomatoes, onions, and herbs in olive oil.
technique_notes: Soften sliced onions ~7 min, add garlic and canned whole tomatoes, break them up and simmer 10-15 min until thickened. Season the fish and squeeze lemon over it, then nestle into the sauce and spoon sauce on top. Bake at 400F just until it flakes (15-25 min). Finish with parsley and more lemon.

name: Caprese Farro Salad
summary: Toss cooked farro with tomatoes, a little fresh mozzarella, and basil in a balsamic dressing.
technique_notes: Boil farro in salted water about 20 min, then strain and rinse with cold water so it cools before mixing. Tear the basil by hand and chop the mozzarella; combine with quartered cherry tomatoes and finish with good olive oil, salt, and pepper. Serve right away or refrigerate.

name: Minestrone Soup
summary: Simmer a vegetable, bean, and small-pasta soup in a light tomato base with herbs.
technique_notes: Saute the onion-carrot-celery soffritto ~8 min, add garlic, then tomatoes, beans, and broth and simmer covered 20 min. Stir in pasta and cook uncovered ~10 min. If making ahead, cook the pasta separately and add per bowl, since it absorbs the broth as it sits. A parmesan rind adds depth.

name: Ratatouille with White Beans
summary: Stew eggplant, zucchini, peppers, and tomato; fold in white beans for a protein-rich main.
technique_notes: Cook each vegetable in stages so each browns instead of stewing: onion+pepper 5-7 min, then eggplant 4-6 min until browned in places, then zucchini 3-5 min, removing each. Return everything with the white beans and tomatoes, cover, and cook 8-10 min just until tender.

name: Salmon Patties with Lemon Yogurt over Greens
summary: Pan-sear herbed salmon patties; serve over dressed greens with a lemon-yogurt sauce.
technique_notes: Flake cooled cooked salmon, bind with egg and crushed crackers, and mix gently until just combined so it stays tender. Form patties, coat, and refrigerate about 1 hour so they hold together. Pan-fry in oil and butter over medium, undisturbed, about 7-8 min per side until golden and crisp.

name: Chicken Shawarma Bowl
summary: Roast shawarma-spiced chicken; build bowls with brown rice, chopped salad, and tahini sauce.
technique_notes: Toss the thighs with the shawarma spices, lemon, and olive oil; refrigerate a couple hours or overnight if you have time. Sear in a cast-iron skillet over medium, spread out, ~5-6 min, then toss and cook another 5-6 min, going longer for browned, crusted edges. Rest before slicing thin.

name: Harissa Chicken with Couscous
summary: Roast harissa-glazed chicken and peppers; serve over whole wheat couscous with herbs.
technique_notes: Couscous is steamed: pour 2 cups boiling stock per 1 cup couscous, cover off the heat, rest 5 min, then fluff and stir in herbs. Sear the spiced chicken hard for char on both sides, then baste with harissa and move to indirect heat to finish to 165F so the glaze doesn't burn. Rest 10 min, slice on the bias.

name: Za'atar Roasted Chicken Thighs with Vegetables
summary: Sheet-pan roast za'atar chicken with tomatoes and onion; finish with lemon.
technique_notes: Roast at 425F: massage za'atar-garlic-lemon oil into the meat and under the skin, nestle thighs among the vegetables, cover with foil ~25 min, then uncover ~30 min until skin browns and crisps. Rest 5-10 min; finish with parsley and a pinch more za'atar.

name: Greek Yogurt Chicken Salad Wrap
summary: Bind shredded chicken with yogurt, celery, and herbs; roll into a whole wheat wrap with greens.
technique_notes: Use poached or roasted chicken cooled before mixing, and pat the add-ins dry so the wrap doesn't get soggy. Layer greens against the wrap as a moisture barrier, or assemble just before eating.

name: Hummus and Roasted Veggie Power Bowl
summary: Top quinoa with hummus, roasted vegetables, and chickpeas; drizzle with lemon-tahini.
technique_notes: Roast the vegetables until caramelized; cool components if packing for lunch. Rinse quinoa to wash off bitter saponins, simmer 1 cup quinoa in 1.75 cups water ~15 min, then rest covered 10 min and fluff. Store parts separately and assemble cold. Thin tahini with lemon and water to drizzle.

name: Lightened Chicken Tikka Masala
summary: Simmer yogurt-marinated chicken in a tomato-spice sauce lightened with yogurt; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Marinate chicken in spiced salted yogurt, but don't over-marinate (4-5 hrs max; the yogurt/lemon acids start cooking the meat). Broil or grill flesh-up ~8 min until charred but still raw inside, rest 10 min, then finish in the simmering sauce ~10 min. Char the aromatics for smoky depth.

name: Palak Chana (Spinach and Chickpea Curry)
summary: Simmer chickpeas in a pureed spinach-ginger-spice sauce; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Dry-toast cumin seeds ~1 min until popping. Build a browned aromatic base, then add ground spices and cook ~2 min before the tomatoes and chickpeas; simmer ~10 min. Stir spinach in only at the very end and just wilt it off the heat to keep it green. Flavor deepens if made ahead.

name: Vegetable Bibimbap
summary: Top brown rice with sauteed and seasoned vegetables and a fried egg; serve with a light gochujang sauce.
technique_notes: Season each vegetable separately rather than together. Sauté carrots in sesame oil 1-2 min; wilt spinach ~30 sec, then squeeze out excess water so the bowl isn't watery. Crisp the rice in a hot pan, arrange veg in sections around a runny-yolk egg, then break the yolk and mix to bind.

name: Thai Red Curry with Tofu and Vegetables
summary: Simmer tofu and vegetables in a red curry with light coconut milk; serve over brown rice.
technique_notes: Press the tofu first. Sauté onion and pepper, then cook the curry paste with ginger ~2 min until fragrant before adding coconut milk; simmer ~10 min until vegetables are tender-crisp. Don't skip the sugar - it balances the paste. Add lime, tofu and basil off the heat.

name: Chicken Adobo
summary: Braise chicken in soy, vinegar, garlic, and bay until tender; serve over brown rice with greens.
technique_notes: Sear the chicken first, then toast garlic, bay and peppercorns in the rendered fat 30-60 sec before adding the liquids and scraping up the fond. Once the vinegar is in, let it simmer before stirring. Simmer uncovered ~20 min to 165F, then broil ~3 min per side for crisp skin.

name: Chili-Lime Shrimp Tacos with Slaw
summary: Sear chili-lime shrimp; tuck into tortillas with a crunchy cabbage-lime slaw and avocado.
technique_notes: Sear the seasoned shrimp hot and fast, just until firm and opaque (~3-5 min), then pull off the heat so they don't overcook. Toast the tortillas in a dry skillet until the edges brown - it deepens flavor and keeps them from tearing. Dress the slaw only just before serving so it stays crunchy.

name: Cuban Black Beans and Brown Rice
summary: Simmer black beans with sofrito and cumin; serve over brown rice with a squeeze of lime.
technique_notes: Build a sofrito: sauté onion and green pepper ~5 min until wilted, then garlic ~1 min until fragrant. Simmer the beans slowly and uncovered until very tender for a creamy texture, adding the sofrito and vinegar partway through. Mash a few beans to thicken; brighten with vinegar at the end.

name: Southwest Quinoa Salad
summary: Toss quinoa with black beans, corn, peppers, and avocado in a cumin-lime dressing.
technique_notes: Rinse the quinoa, then cook and spread it out to cool and dry so it isn't mushy and absorbs the dressing without going gummy. Add the avocado last.

name: Greek Turkey Burgers with Tzatziki
summary: Grill turkey burgers studded with feta and spinach; top with cucumber-yogurt tzatziki.
technique_notes: Squeeze the spinach dry, don't overmix, and give lean turkey a binder (feta, a little oil) for moisture. Press a thumbprint dimple in each patty so they don't dome, and don't press them while cooking.

name: Mediterranean Sheet-Pan Chicken and Vegetables
summary: Roast chicken with seasonal vegetables, olive oil, oregano, and lemon on one pan.
technique_notes: Cut veg by density and spread in a single uncrowded layer so each piece touches the hot pan and chars instead of steaming. Toss with lemon-oregano-garlic dressing; roast thighs at 425°F about 35 min to 165°F, then broil a couple minutes for color. For chicken breast, cube and roast at 400°F ~20 min.

name: Balela (Mediterranean Chickpea and Bean Salad)
summary: Toss chickpeas and beans with tomato, parsley, and mint in a lemon-olive oil dressing.
technique_notes: Dry the herbs and beans well, then toss with a zesty olive oil, lemon juice, white wine vinegar, garlic and sumac dressing. Leave it aside at least 30 minutes so flavors meld before serving. Best at room temperature, though it can be covered and chilled until ready.

name: Sicilian Cauliflower Pasta
summary: Roast cauliflower and toss with pasta, a little raisin and pine nut, garlic, and chili.
technique_notes: Deeply brown the cauliflower for nutty flavor (traditional versions simmer it tender, then break it into a sauce). Plump raisins, bloom saffron and soften toasted pine nuts in the starchy cooking water, finish pasta just shy of al dente in the pan, and top with toasted breadcrumbs for crunch.

name: Misir Wot (Ethiopian Red Lentil Stew)
summary: Simmer red lentils with onion and berbere into a richly spiced stew; serve with greens and brown rice.
technique_notes: Cook the onions long and dry (little to no oil at first) until jammy before adding the berbere, then bloom the berbere in oil. Simmer the red lentils until they fully break down and thicken.

name: Harira (Moroccan Lentil and Chickpea Soup)
summary: Simmer lentils and chickpeas in a spiced tomato base finished with lemon and cilantro.
technique_notes: Soften onion, celery and carrot in olive oil, then bloom the spices 1-2 min. Add crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, lentils, chickpeas and cilantro; simmer ~45 min until legumes are very tender, adjusting liquid so it stays pourable. Thicken near the end with broken vermicelli or rice; finish with lemon.

name: Gigantes Plaki (Greek Baked Giant Beans)
summary: Bake large white beans in a tomato-herb sauce until creamy; serve with greens and feta.
technique_notes: Pre-cook (or use canned) giant/butter beans, then build a chunky tomato sauce by softening onion, carrot, celery and garlic before adding tomatoes and herbs. Simmer the beans in it briefly, then bake uncovered at 375°F for 20-30 min until thickened and the top turns golden.

name: Grilled Chicken Skewers with Chimichurri
summary: Grill chicken skewers and vegetables; spoon over a bright herb chimichurri.
technique_notes: Make the chimichurri chunky by hand (not a smooth blender puree) and let it rest 20+ min to meld. Don't crowd the skewers, grill hot for char, and rest the chicken before serving.

name: Seared Tuna Niçoise-Style Plate
summary: Sear tuna rare; plate with blanched green beans, potatoes, egg, and a dijon vinaigrette.
technique_notes: Tuna is best rare: sear a good steak about a minute per side over very high heat and slice it against the grain - it turns dry and chalky if cooked through. Blanch and cook the other components separately and compose the plate.

name: Pan-Seared Halibut with Romesco
summary: Sear halibut and serve over a roasted red pepper, tomato, and almond romesco sauce.
technique_notes: Halibut is lean and dries out fast: pat it bone-dry, sear in a hot pan undisturbed until it releases on its own, and pull it at just-opaque since it carries over off the heat. Romesco is blended from roasted peppers and tomato with toasted almonds and a little bread for body - make it ahead, it improves as it sits.

name: South Indian Fish Curry (Meen Kuzhambu)
summary: Simmer white fish in a tangy tomato-tamarind and light-coconut curry with South Indian spices.
technique_notes: Build and simmer the curry base fully before the fish goes in, then slip the fillets in and poach gently - boiling toughens fish and breaks it apart. Bloom mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil first (they should splutter). Add the tamarind near the end and don't over-reduce once the fish is in.

name: Thai Steamed Fish with Lime, Garlic, and Chili
summary: Steam white fish over aromatics and finish with a punchy raw garlic-lime-chili dressing.
technique_notes: Steam just until the fish flakes (about 8-10 min depending on thickness) - steaming is unforgiving of overcooking, so check early. Make the lime-garlic-chili-fish-sauce dressing raw and spoon it over after steaming so it stays bright and sharp; don't cook it.

name: Shrimp Saganaki (Greek Shrimp with Tomato and Feta)
summary: Bake shrimp in a garlicky tomato sauce topped with feta until just pink and bubbling.
technique_notes: Reduce the tomato sauce until thick before the shrimp go in, then add the shrimp and cook only until they turn pink and curl into a C - they keep cooking in the hot sauce, so pull early. Marinate the shrimp in oil, oregano, dill, and garlic first; simmer the sauce 15 min; sprinkle feta on at the end off-heat.

name: Cajun Blackened Tilapia with Corn and Black Beans
summary: Coat tilapia in Cajun spice and sear hard for a blackened crust; serve with a corn and black bean salad.
technique_notes: Blackening needs a screaming-hot cast-iron pan and a dry, well-spiced fillet: press the paprika-cayenne-thyme rub on and let it sit (up to 30 min). Heat oil until almost smoking; don't move the fillet until the crust sets (about 3 min per side). Tilapia is thin and cooks fast, so flip only once. Use good ventilation.

name: Spanish Mussels in Smoked-Paprika Tomato Broth
summary: Steam mussels open in a smoky tomato, garlic, and white-wine broth.
technique_notes: Scrub the mussels and discard any that stay open when tapped before cooking, and any that stay shut after. Build the tomato-paprika broth first, then add the mussels, cover, and steam just until they open (4-6 min) - pull them as they open so they don't turn rubbery. Bloom the smoked paprika briefly off high heat so it doesn't scorch.

name: Sicilian Swordfish with Tomato, Caper, and Mint
summary: Grill or sear swordfish and top with a quick Sicilian tomato, caper, olive, and mint relish.
technique_notes: Swordfish dries out if overcooked, so use thick steaks (1-1.5 in). Dredge in flour for color, then use unilateral cooking: brown hard on the first side ~5 min, flip only ~2 min to 130-135F. Build the tomato-caper-olive sauce in the same pan, then nestle the fish back to warm through. Keep the relish bright, not over-reduced.

name: Roasted Cauliflower With Feta, Almonds and Olives
summary: Roast cauliflower until deeply browned; toss with feta, toasted almonds, and olives.
technique_notes: Spread cauliflower in a single uncrowded layer and roast at 425°F without stirring too often so the florets actually brown rather than steam. Add feta and olives after roasting so the feta softens but doesn't fully melt, and toast the almonds separately so they stay crunchy.

name: Kale and Butternut Squash Bowl With Jammy Eggs
summary: Roast butternut squash, sauté kale, and serve over grains with jammy soft-boiled eggs and a tahini drizzle.
technique_notes: Roast squash at 425°F cut-side down first for caramelization, then flip. For jammy eggs, lower into boiling water and cook exactly 7 minutes, then shock in ice water. Massage kale with a little oil and lemon to soften it before sautéing.

name: Cherry Tomato and White Bean Salad
summary: Marinate cherry tomatoes and white beans in olive oil, red wine vinegar, and basil; serve at room temperature.
technique_notes: Halve the cherry tomatoes and toss raw with rinsed cannellini, chopped basil, and good EVOO - no cooking. Use a robust extra-virgin olive oil; its flavor carries the dish. Drizzle aged balsamic and flaky salt at the very end, just before serving. Serve at room temperature; keeps about 2 days though basil may discolor.

name: Lemony Asparagus Salad With Shaved Cheese and Nuts
summary: Shave raw or blanched asparagus thin, toss with lemon vinaigrette, and top with shaved hard cheese and toasted nuts.
technique_notes: Use a vegetable peeler to shave raw asparagus into ribbons for a delicate texture, or blanch briefly (1-2 min) and shock in ice water for something more tender. Dress with lemon right before serving since the acid wilts the ribbons fast. Toast the nuts dry in a pan.

name: Mediterranean Fish Chowder With Potatoes and Kale
summary: Simmer white fish and potatoes in a light tomato-fennel broth with kale.
technique_notes: Cook the potatoes fully in the broth before adding fish, since the fish only needs 5-8 min and overcooks quickly. Strip kale from tough stems and add it a few minutes before the fish. A splash of white wine and fennel seed in the broth define the Mediterranean character.

name: Mackerel With Lemon Olive Oil and Tomatoes
summary: Roast or pan-sear mackerel and serve over garlicky burst tomatoes with lemon and herbs.
technique_notes: Mackerel is oily and robust — it handles high heat well. Score the skin to prevent curling, then sear skin-side down first in a very hot pan. Burst the tomatoes in olive oil and garlic in a separate pan, and finish with lemon and parsley off the heat so the herbs stay bright.

name: Citrusy Roast Chicken With Pears and Figs
summary: Roast chicken thighs over sweet pears and figs with lemon and fresh thyme until caramelized.
technique_notes: Use ripe but firm pears so they don't turn to mush. Nestle fruit around (not under) the chicken so it can brown properly; the fruit juices mingle with the chicken fat to create a pan sauce. Add dried figs partway through rather than at the start so they don't burn.

name: Cucumber-Tomato Salad With Seared Halloumi and Olive Oil Croutons
summary: Sear sliced halloumi golden, toss with cucumber-tomato salad, and top with crunchy olive oil croutons.
technique_notes: Sear halloumi in a dry (no oil) very hot pan — it has enough fat — for 1-2 min per side until deeply golden; serve immediately as it toughens as it cools. Salt and drain the cucumber briefly first. Make the croutons last so they stay crunchy.

name: Greens and Beans With Toasted Crumbs
summary: Sauté hearty greens and white beans in garlicky olive oil; top with crispy pan-toasted breadcrumbs.
technique_notes: Fry torn bread or coarse crumbs in olive oil until golden and salty, then set them aside — add at the very last second or they go soggy. Mash some of the beans against the pan to create a creamy, thickened sauce, and wilt the greens fully in the bean liquid.

name: Farro With Blistered Tomatoes, Pesto and Spinach
summary: Blister cherry tomatoes in olive oil, toss with cooked farro, pesto, and fresh spinach.
technique_notes: Blister the tomatoes in a very hot dry skillet or under a broiler so they char and burst, adding sweetness. Toss everything together off the heat so the pesto stays green and the spinach just wilts from residual warmth. Farro holds up well at room temp, so this works as a warm grain salad.

name: Slow-Roasted Citrus Salmon With Herb Salad
summary: Slow-roast a whole salmon fillet in olive oil with citrus slices; top with a bright herb salad.
technique_notes: Low and slow (275°F, 25-30 min) produces silky, barely-set salmon that's completely different in texture from high-heat roasting. The fish is done when it just starts to flake and loses translucency. Build the herb salad (parsley, dill, tarragon, thinly sliced shallot, lemon juice) right before serving.

name: Saffron Salmon Kababs
summary: Marinate salmon in saffron, lemon, and onion, then grill or broil on skewers.
technique_notes: Bloom the saffron in a tablespoon of warm water for 10-15 min to extract its color and flavor before adding to the marinade. Don't marinate more than 1 hour or the lemon will start to denature the fish. Grill or broil hot and fast so the salmon gets color without drying out.

name: Roasted Halibut With Lemons, Olives and Rosemary
summary: Roast halibut over a bed of lemon slices, olives, and rosemary until just cooked through.
technique_notes: Halibut is lean and dries out quickly — roast at 400°F and check early (10-12 min for 1-inch fillets). Roasting on sliced lemons keeps the fish elevated and fragrant. Go easy on salt since the olives are already salty. Pull the fish when it's just barely opaque all the way through.

name: Salmon and Couscous Salad With Cucumber-Feta Dressing
summary: Roast salmon and serve over couscous with a creamy blended cucumber-feta dressing and herbs.
technique_notes: Couscous is ready in 5 minutes: pour boiling salted liquid over it (1:1 ratio), cover and rest, then fluff. Blend the dressing smooth (cucumber, feta, lemon, a little yogurt or olive oil) and taste for salt before adding — feta varies. Let the couscous cool slightly before assembling so the dressing doesn't break.

name: Simmered Beet Greens With Roasted Beets, Lemon and Yogurt
summary: Roast beets and simmer their greens separately; serve together over garlicky yogurt with lemon.
technique_notes: Roast the beets wrapped in foil until a knife slides in easily (45-60 min at 400°F), then slip the skins off while warm. Simmer the greens (stems first, then leaves) briefly in salted water and drain well — they're more tender than kale but need a few minutes. The yogurt base is the sauce: season it with garlic and lemon.

name: Puttanesca Chickpea-Tomato Salad
summary: Toss chickpeas and tomatoes with olives, capers, and anchovies in a bold puttanesca vinaigrette.
technique_notes: The anchovies melt into the dressing if you whisk them into the oil — they add savory depth without a fishy flavor, and you can omit them for fully vegetarian. Let the salad sit 10-15 min after dressing so the chickpeas absorb the bold flavors. Good at room temperature or slightly warm.

name: Italian Wedding Soup
summary: Simmer chicken meatballs with orzo and vegetables in a light broth; finish with baby spinach and parmesan.
technique_notes: Build the soup base by cooking onion, carrot, celery, and garlic in olive oil until translucent (4-5 min) before adding broth. Cook the orzo directly in the broth (not separately) and pull it when just tender — about 9 min — before the meatballs go in. Add meatballs and baby spinach together at the very end and cook only 2-4 min; spinach needs no chopping and wilts almost instantly. Make meatballs larger than marble-size (easier to form and more satisfying). Batch-make and freeze meatballs ahead so the soup comes together in 20 min. Finish with a generous drizzle of olive oil and parmesan at the table.

name: High-Protein Caprese Chickpea Salad
summary: Toss chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, and mozzarella in a Dijon-balsamic vinaigrette with fresh basil.
technique_notes: The dressing is the key: whisk balsamic vinegar, olive oil, Dijon mustard, and grated (not minced) raw garlic — the Dijon emulsifies and the grated garlic melts in without chunks. For added texture, toast half the chickpeas in a dry pan until crispy and toss them in at the end so they stay crunchy. Use pearl mozzarella whole; it holds its shape and size better than torn fresh mozzarella. The salad holds well for up to 3 days refrigerated, making it ideal for meal prep — add basil just before serving.

name: Chickpea & Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Red Pepper Sauce
summary: Build grain bowls with quinoa and chickpeas topped with a blended roasted red pepper, almond, and spice sauce.
technique_notes: The sauce is the dish: blend jarred roasted red peppers with slivered almonds, olive oil, garlic, paprika, and cumin until fairly smooth — it's similar to romesco but lighter (no bread, more cumin). If it feels too thick, add a splash of water. Make the sauce and the seasoned quinoa base separately ahead of time, then assemble just before serving so the components stay distinct. Toss the cooked, cooled quinoa with kalamata olives, red onion, and olive oil to season it before plating.

name: One-Skillet Garlicky Salmon and Broccoli
summary: Sear salmon pieces with garlic, set aside, then cook broccoli and peppers in the same pan; finish with orange juice and tamari.
technique_notes: Use a nonstick skillet so the salmon releases cleanly. Cook salmon pieces in a single layer with half the sliced garlic over medium-high heat 4-5 min, stirring occasionally, then transfer to a plate — don't wipe the pan so the salmon flavor stays. Add broccoli, bell peppers, the remaining garlic, and a tablespoon of water; cover and cook 4-5 min until just tender-crisp. Cut broccoli into bite-sized pieces so it cooks through in time. Stir in orange juice and tamari off the heat, then fold salmon back in gently so it doesn't break apart. Request center-cut salmon at the fish counter for uniform thickness. Salmon is done at 130-135°F (it carries over to 145°F off heat).

name: White Bean Salad With Roasted Cauliflower
summary: Roast cauliflower until caramelized, toss with white beans, herbs, and a bright lemon dressing.
technique_notes: Roast cauliflower at high heat (425°F) in a single uncrowded layer until deeply browned — the caramelization is what makes this dish. Toss the warm cauliflower with the beans right away so the beans absorb some warmth and the dressing, then let it cool to room temperature before adding fresh herbs.
